main_issue: Only the CVE-2022-24897 anchors substantiate a Velocity sandbox/introspection-policy gap; the CVE-2022-23621 evidence is explicitly retrieval ground truth rather than vulnerability-mechanism evidence, so the two cases do not yet support the broad privileged-capability-exposure guideline.
evidence_notes: CVE-2022-24897: SecureUberspector/SecureIntrospector and default Velocity sandbox registration support a dynamic-template security-boundary mechanism, but the supplied trace does not establish a lower-privilege caller reaching a privileged API without an entry-point authorization check.
CVE-2022-23621: anchors only identify invokeServletAndReturnAsString review windows; no source, sink, missing guard, exploit precondition, or patch-side behavior is provided.

The cluster summary lists several distinct possible mechanisms—script-right checks, method whitelists, document-origin validation, and content-type defaults—which require patch-backed case evidence before they can be combined or split reliably.
